select_exclusion() implements the R104 rule: take the top delete-one shift-norm patch in curvature row 0, then the top row-1 patch that differs from it, both computed on the data set's own all-48 delete-one refits. Three sector variants are implemented: EB (E2+B2 10-dim, primary), B2 and E2. On the observed data all three select (8,47); fail closed otherwise. Each of the 6000 cached draws was replayed and given its own selection. The excl null tables (configs.excl_selected__*) and exclusion_ratio_selected_over_all48 use this selection, and ratio_rule_spread gives the per-rule counts next to the fixed value. Fixed-(8,47) tables are kept only under fixed_patch_conditional_diagnostic, with a scope string. The matched rules pick (8,47) itself in 0-1.8% of draws, with 323-553 distinct pairs per null.

The docstring now describes 8/47 as the top patches for row 0 (every sector) and for row-1 E2/B2, notes that 32 is the top row-1 glide/spin patch, and notes that (43,47) is the worst delete-two pair in 7 of 8 row-sectors. observed.json replays the R104 top-5 and worst-pair lists from the R98 cache and asserts they match GAIA_PATCH_INFLUENCE.json. It also reports observed-only statistics for the exclusions {32}, {43,47}, {8,47,32}, {8,47,43} and {8,47,32,43}; across these, spin6 jk1 changes by at most 5.59% relative to all48.

Docstring restricted to frames evaluated at the shell medians. The key was renamed to shell_median_affine_frame_rhs_injection_max_abs (3.4e-14) and now carries a scope string. A new direct per-source injection of the R105 test frame through group_normal gives: shell-median leak 8.8e-14; per-source leak max 1.3136 uas/yr/z^2 (all48) and 1.3233 (excl). At the default 1.0 the output is bit-identical: 100 nominal mocks per family replay the 2000-mock deltas and t_self exactly (max diff 0.0). New helpers: l1_dipole_xy (healpy sign convention checked by the test), offdiag_fraction_contrast, closed_form_cov, c1_crossing_gaussian, tself_coefficients / c1_crossing_mc. The c1zero stage ran 1000 C_1=0 mocks per DIFF family on the main-run seeds, so each is a common-random-number (CRN) partner of a reference mock. The report gives p versus C_1 two ways. (i) Gaussian closed form: Cov = Cov_{C1=0}(mocks) + df^2 (3C_1/4pi) I_2, with df = 0.07446 from the observed joint class counts. (ii) A semi-analytic p_mc for the R65 t_self statistic, adding df*sqrt(C_1)*u_i, where u_i is each mock's own unit l=1 dipole. The closed form was validated against the reference ensemble at C_1=A_m (per mock) and against direct 500-mock runs at the 0.05 crossing. The report gives the 0.05 and 0.01 crossings with bootstrap 16-84% intervals. The docstring and scope now restate each null as an assumed resolved-fraction dipole of RMS sqrt(3C_1/4pi). They forbid quoting any family's p as the LSS/selection-null p, and say C_1=0 is not a conservative limit (Cov0 is still 1.97-2.77x Poisson). Scoped, not fixed: C_1 is not anchored by external data. The semi-analytic k(C_1) is not monotone on the grid for RED/MID because of MC step noise; the first crossing is reported and flagged.

MID is no longer called 'data-preferred' or 'favoured' anywhere in code or outputs (grep for 'preferred' over the script, follow-up JSONs and RUN_RECORD: 0 hits). The label had only appeared in prose. The shape_selector() output reports MID only as the family whose NSIDE8/4 contrast ratio is closest to the data. It gives the 9-mock z-scores (RED +1.36, MID -0.59, FLAT -1.74, COMMON -3.06), which exclude no DIFF family. It also gives the full range of reference p(t_self, dipole): FLAT 0.012, MID 0.17, RED 0.57. Insensitivity to C_1 was rechecked on the reference seeds. On 12 calibration seeds the jk4 contrast trace at C_1=0 divided by nominal is 1.005 (RED), 0.999 (MID), 1.018 (FLAT). On 9 scale seeds the 8/4 ratio at C_1=0 versus nominal is 0.580 vs 0.583 (RED), 0.715 vs 0.712 (MID), 0.852 vs 0.848 (FLAT).

The amplitude stage ran 40 new jk4+estimator mocks per family on seeds [ROOT_SEED,300,i] and pooled them with the 21 reference values. Amplitude spread: SD_A = SD(trace)/(target-base) = 0.272 (RED), 0.231 (MID), 0.212 (FLAT). It was combined in quadrature with the 12-mock calibration SE (0.092, 0.096, 0.077), giving sigma_r = 0.287, 0.250, 0.225. The nuisance is treated as independent. Spearman correlation of the jk4 trace with t_self over the 40 new mocks is -0.13, -0.11, -0.11; this is a weak check at that n. Marginal p comes from 800 mocks per family, each drawing its own amplitude r_i ~ N(1, sigma_r) truncated at r > 0 (deterministic seeds). The 16-84% band comes from fixed 500-mock ensembles at the r16 and r84 quantiles. The report shows p to 2 significant figures with counts and MC SEs, instead of 4-digit p_mc. Scoped: the band is conditional on each family's shape, with C_1 = r*A_m.

corrected_headline_results: CONDITIONAL PREDICTION. Every DIFF-family null p is conditional on the l=1 power C_1 of the differential field, which the NSIDE4/8 jackknife cannot see. CONDITIONAL PREDICTION. Closed form Cov = Cov_{C1=0} + df^2 (3C_1/4pi) I_2 with df = 0.0745 (observed counts). Applied to t_self (dipole), p crosses 0.05 at C_1 = 1.62e-3 [1.51, 1.78]e-3 (RED, 0.089 A_m), 2.06e-3 [1.90, 2.18]e-3 (MID, 0.45 A_m) and 2.39e-3 [2.19, 2.57]e-3 (FLAT, 1.88 A_m). findings_addressed.detail: Four exclusion sets are now flagged as defined by apparent magnitude: 2MRS_galaxy, 2MRS_coras_input, complement_keep_only_2MRS_coras_input, and union_2MRS_coras_or_CF3_window. Each block also stores a mark_zero_point_confound record: the kept-set inverse-variance mean delta_d against the same control masks, overall and per 2000 km/s bin, plus the mean epsilon_d. Each set gets a comparability record with a citation rule (f=0 fractions are not overlap or leakage evidence) and an 'unresolved residual' statement. A new block, drop_recentered_czbin, removes the zero point per 2000 km/s cz bin using the selected training rows; it is scored against cz x inclusion controls and, as a separate block, against cz x inclusion x epsilon_d-quintile controls (drop_recentered_czbin_eps_strata). The member/non-member zero-point split now reports chi2 heterogeneity, an error inflated by sqrt(chi2/dof), and an exact velocity equivalent labelled as selection-induced, not a flow.

Every CORAS scorer now has a coras_conditioning record. It states that the scores are conditional on fsigma8=0.405 and bulk (95,-172,28) km/s and sets held_out_with_respect_to_cf3_calibration=false. It also holds the bulk decomposition (offset_only, bulk_only, bulk_removed, as_run), checked against the replay to 1e-8, and a parameter-sensitivity bound computed in this run: bulk shifted by +/- eTot and +/- eDist per axis, fsigma8 shifted by +/- eTot and +/- eDist, the in-sample 6dF-preferred bulk, and B_other for the velocity and mu 6dF shares. The CF3_calibration_window fold now has a scope_note: it scores only 160 cz-edge rows (120 selected), cannot bound full-sample leakage, and gives the leakage-proxy-to-control-sd ratio.
